text: Because fast cellular processes equilibrate much more quickly than slow ones, timescale separation allows fast variables to be treated as if they are at quasi-steady-state relative to the slower variables.
explanation: This is true and is the core principle behind timescale separation: as the ratio of fast to slow timescales becomes extreme, the fast variable can be approximated as always being at its steady-state value given the current (slowly changing) value of the slow variable. This principle underlies simplifications such as the Michaelis-Menten approximation for enzyme kinetics and the treatment of fast ion-channel gates in Hodgkin-Huxley-type models.
